notes.title: Dead in Vinland dumps a viking family on North America's shore
notes.notes:
Maybe the phrase "turn-based resource management game" doesn't get you excited. Let me summarize Dead in Vinland a different way—it's a game about helping a family of lost vikings who are shipwrecked on the distant shores of what is probably Canada. That's a unique setup for a survival game, but it's not just the setup that makes Dead in Vinland interesting.

Survival games are often annoying because you spend all your time time scarfing down food and water to keep hunger and thirst meters out of the red, in between frantically punching trees to gather wood. Dead in Vinland isn't like that. You only have to ration out food and water once per day, and nobody punches a single tree.

Each day is sliced into three parts. The first two are for work, so you assign each survivor to a job in the morning (maybe putting someone down to fish and someone else to hunt), and then again in the afternoon (maybe one to cook the meat gathered in the morning, while others craft or explore or rest). Then at night everyone gathers around the campfire to eat and talk, little visual novel conversations that deepen the relationships between characters. You might learn that free-spirited daughter Kari doesn't respect her mother, a Welsh freedwoman who is a bit of a homebody, but adores her father, a guilt-racked berserk.

These quiet times are also opportunities to delve into the new land's mysteries—chief among them, an odd blue woman who might be a goddess. But there are also survivors of a suspicious number of other shipwrecks around, and a whole gang of jerks who demand regular tribute. It's a strange new land full of strange new people.

If you've tried CCCP's previous game Dead in Bermuda this might sound familiar, even down to the blue-skinned deities, but Dead in Vinland improves on that game in plenty of ways. One is the art style, which is a bit reminiscent of The Banner Saga and makes picking up and putting down these little people feel like playing with well-modeled figurines. It's also a lot easier to read at a glance than Bermuda, with icons that make it simpler to keep track of who is tired and who is depressed—although the icon for depression being a noose seems in poor taste.

The biggest difference between the two games is that Dead in Vinland has combat. Your vikings and their opponents line up in two rows and take it in turns spending action points to wail on each other in the traditional way. Some characters do well in the front rank, like Blodeuwedd with her shieldmaiden-style ability to guard allies, while Kari is better sniping from the back with her bow. There are interesting decisions to be made even with positioning this limited—Kari's taunt ability provides a nice debuff, but using it forces her into the front row, for instance.

After 18 days of fighting people with axes and grimly scraping a living out of the wilderness, I overworked Eirik the berserk and he died of fatigue. It's an instant game over when any of the core family members die, which I prefer to the protracted failure cascade of Dead in Bermuda—someone would die and it would depress someone else so much they walked off a cliff, which would depress someone else so much they'd follow, and so on. 

Instead, Dead in Vinland is over fast. You get a summary of how well you did and then you can just reload from that morning to try again. Permadeath's an option but I'm happier without it. This is a story I'd like to see unfold rather than reading the opening chapter again and again till I get it right. I just hope it has a better ending than Dead in Bermuda did, but I'll have to make it a lot further than day 18 to find out.

One thing that still needs some work is its writing. There are plenty of intriguing characters, but when the enigmatic witch greets me with, "Eating too much flies with you big mouth open like this?" I wince. 

Everything else about It feels solid. It seems like survival games have finally escaped from the doldrums this year, with Subnautica and Frostpunk avoiding the genre's typical problems and finding new things to do with the toolset. Dead in Vinland is shaping up to join them, another game discovering a way to take a tired genre and reset its fatigue meter.

notes.title: Dead in Vinland - Traits
notes.notes:
Hello survivors! 

Today, we’re going to talk about [b]traits[/b] in Dead in Vinland. 
In Dead in Vinland, we have several types of traits:[b]
•	Historical & random traits that are available at the start of a new game.
•	Traits that you gain throughout the game
•	Temporary traits
•	Traits that are diseases/wounds
[/b]
Before going further, let’s explain [b]what a trait is[/b]. [b]A trait is a characteristic that is given to each character[/b]. They will have many effects. They can for instance give a bonus of XP or decrease the skills of a character.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/67ad9aac107e5a5805906d0b0f2faacf448c5584.png[/img]

Finally, the traits can be either [b]good[/b] or [b]bad[/b] for the character. Hence, there are [b]2 columns[/b] in the traits menu: traits in the [b]green column[/b] will give a [b]bonus[/b] to the character, while those in the [b]red[/b] one will give him/her a [b]penalty[/b].

Now, we’ll talk about the [b]historical and random traits[/b] at the start of the game. As you know, each character has his/her own personality. For example, in the game, Eirik blames himself for what happened to his family, and Kari loves adventures. Well, that has an impact in the game! Each character has [b]one good[/b] and [b]one bad historical trait[/b] when you start the game.

It’s kind of contradictory, because the backstory and physical characteristics of characters give you strong constraints that will stick to this character. For example, an old man couldn’t have the skills of a strong, fierce young man. Things like that. So, we must deal with FIXED, logical characteristics for characters, and add a little randomness whenever it’s possible.

That’s why in Dead in Vinland [b]each character starts[/b] with a set of [b]HISTORIC traits[/b], that are fixed and tailored for [b]him/her only[/b], and a set of random, lesser characteristics drawn from a pool of traits. [img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/a4b08470dde4e9cff1eb4d267ed7f964a05775f8.png[/img]
[i]Hum, looks like Moira got a “Blessed” trait, and this one could be helpful. How did she get it though?[/i]

Then, let’s mention the temporary traits. They can also be gained in the game, but the difference with the previous ones is that they disappear over time. You’ll also gain them in the game because of your choices (dialogue choices for example).

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/cec2e1f6e169f6dd5c70328b3ac349b2914e8040.gif[/img]
[i]Kari didn’t want to upset her dad, and now she’ll be depressed for 3 days.[/i]

Those traits won’t be as impactful, but you should still be wary of them, as depression is one way to die in Dead in Vinland for example.

Finally, in Dead in Vinland, you can get [b]diseases[/b] or [b]wounds[/b]. Those also count as traits. There are 2 ways to get those. During exploration, when you miss a skill check for example.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/01aec56a67cef35e703311b445b60e7ebdbe2f66.png[/img]
[i]Eirik shouldn’t have pushed himself so far.[/i]

And finally, as we’ve said in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/573120/announcements/detail/1640870906392990417][b]post about combat[/b][/url], if you lose too much HP in battle, you can get some injuries. Those will count as traits.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/43a37a7c5d83b3100a00fac6091044daeb9b01ea.png[/img]
[i]Blodeuwedd’s arm will take 5 days to heal.[/i]

And that’s a wrap about traits! As you saw, there will be many traits in Dead in Vinland, and some will be quite beneficial (the green column), others will add penalties to the characters, and the player will have a harder time to survive. But it will be fun. We promise. Happy surviving!

notes.title: About the Characters - Secondary characters #2
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/3ac80bce74930aef627ebf19c3e2c8f89109f2ad.png[/img]

We’ll present today 3 other [b]secondary characters[/b] that you’ll maybe find when [b]exploring the island[/b]. Those three are known for having a [b]natural charisma[/b] but are quite [b]hard to figure out[/b] on first encounter. They could be very good allies if you understand their [b]specificities[/b] & [b]behaviours[/b].

                                             [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/96ad26101409445be178450ec959f722435caa30.png[/img]

[b]Eustache[/b]
[i]The Black Monk[/i]

We'll start with Eustache, youngest son of a [b]french noble family[/b]. The path to his father’s titles barred by his older brothers, his mother sent him to the benedictine monks.

He left the abbey after his father’s assassination, with only [b]bitterness[/b] and [b]vengeance[/b] in his pockets. He [b]exiled[/b] himself to [b]Spain[/b] to study fencing, and some say, [b]black magic[/b]. He then enlisted at the service of the Count of Boulogne, to whom he demanded justice for his father.

But he faced the harsh truth of noble schemes and [b]lost his trial[/b], meaning all his land and titles, to the filthy Count.

He gutted him clean and well. Then he wrecked havoc on the northern seas as a [b]pirate[/b] known as the [b]Black Monk[/b]. His reign of terror lasted a good decade before he entered in a terrible fight with a viking longship, leaving him for dead on a drifting piece of wood. He wrecked on the island, more dead than alive.

                                             [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/da40d1d1ce9935286567538e8b4910f3dda91ea2.png[/img]

[b]Shanaw[/b]
[i]Beothuk Huntress[/i]

Shanaw was the [b]daughter[/b] of the [b]chief[/b] of the [b]Beothuk tribe[/b], a small native village living on an island not far from the island of Dead In Vinland.

A [b]free spirit[/b], she was an [b]excellent hunter[/b] and [b]runner[/b], and was known amongst her kin for very [b]mischevious behavior[/b]. Her many wacky moments, like dancing and howling naked under the moonlight, earned her the nickname of “[b]Crazy Moon[/b]”.

How did she end up on the island of Eirik and his family? And why? That’s a secret you will have to uncover, even if her shell may be hard to crack.

The only thing we know, is that she took the name of “[b]Hidden Raven[/b]”. And that she doesn’t want to talk to Eirik. Weird.


                                            [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/73220a8a140924b9b34ee8fa0a9078c8e16cf0ac.png[/img]

[b]Yaghoub[/b]
[i]Persian Merchant[/i]

Yaghoub is an appealing [b]Persian Merchant[/b] with a majestuous beard neatly combed and filled with precious jewels. He is always giving you big friendly smiles, always has an incredible story to tell. But despite these classic merchant features, he also shows an [b]astonishing sense of sharing[/b], and an [b]infinite kindness[/b].

Some may think he only works as a greedy merchant to be able to travel the world on his beloved ship. In fact, each time he manages to make a good profit, he instantly spend it all on a new, bigger, longer, riskier expedition, making him the [b]poorest merchant[/b] there is. But when you see this spark in his eyes when he tells a – mostly invented – story, you understand that he carries his true wealth inside his heart.

A [b]terrible storm[/b] made him wreck on the shores of the island of Vinland. He survived alongside a [b]mysterious passenger[/b]…

That's all for today, next time, there will be a special post, [b]quite different[/b] from what you've seen before, so, stay tuned!

notes.title: Fighting for survival
notes.notes:
Hello survivors! Let’s dive today into our [b]fighting system[/b], one of the new features for Dead In Vinland.

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/96d7bc4324689d0ed6cb73a370d59838d6bb4ee0.gif[/img]

Let’s start by the basics.
Dead In Vinland proposes a [b]turn-based[/b] combat system, opposing up to 6 characters [b](3 vs 3)[/b]. We designed our fights in order for them to be [b]tactical[/b], but [b]quick[/b]. It was important that they don’t break the [b]rhythm[/b] of the game, since you will have many things to think about in the management part.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/55a91890ce959b7e3337160a1d10d7a103c78318.png[/img]
 
The battle takes place on a small [b]grid[/b] with [b]back[/b] and [b]front rows[/b]: each party has its side and each character has its associated [b]line[/b] and the skills target characters on specific rows (or on any row). Characters acts one by one considering their [b]INITIATIVE[/b].

             [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/20656185d918e401de2c94ad8ff79ad5b1140bcd.png[/img]

This row system is [b]dynamic[/b], meaning that a front row exists only if there is actually [b]at least one character on the front row[/b], “protecting” his comrades, if there’s no front row, your characters could be hit by any skill!

Each character has Action Points each turn, which he can spend to [b]activate skills[/b], or move. You’ll need to find the optimal use of the Action Points pool of your character to success.

Every character can [b]switch row[/b] using 1 [b]Action Point[/b].

       [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/1ab6b64fc2e723eb0153dbc54394d9e013e6aafe.gif[/img]

End your turn without spending all your Action Points grants you one AP for the following turn.

                                        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/18682e43ea574c44a7dc918718e75df44ff1b662.png[/img]
                                            [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/788f9f8a7bf377d85a3841e36833761af928b7a7.png[/img]

The battle ends when all characters on one side lose all their Health Points. 

Note that we separated the [b]injury state bar[/b] that you have during the game from the actual [b]HP of a fight[/b]. Consider fights’ injuries to be short-term, and injury bar to be long-term. When a character loses all his/her HP, he is [b]Knocked Out[/b].

The HP are divided into 2 rows: above 10 and under 10.

                                        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/cffb068e465a31f38fa8bbff94d2a82de4922c37.png[/img]

Above 10 are “[b]armor[/b]” HP. You can lose them all you want, it won’t have any effect on your injury state. But if your HP go below 10, for each HP lost, the character will gain [b]some injury after the battle ends[/b]. Obviously, 100% injury means the character’s [b]death[/b]!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/536e486b7c69300bdd6f72391266adc5e6f4cdae.png[/img]

Each playable character has a specific Battle Class and a Passive Ability. There are 5 Battle Classes, and each class has a specific purpose in battle
·        [b]Warrior[/b]: Pretty balanced fighter, works best in the front row
·        [b]Protector[/b]: Can shield their weaker allies
·        [b]Shooter[/b]: Damage dealers, in need of protection ; can also reach enemy back rows
·        [b]Mystic[/b]: Can buff and debuff
·        [b]Civilian[/b]: Disrupts the flow of the battle with their chaotic skills (row-changing, large damage range…)
 
The Battle Class determines the set of 5 activable skills the character has in battle.
They will also have a [b]Passive Ability[/b], which is independent from the Battle Class. It acts as a modifier to their behavior. Those different combinations mean [b]each character will have its unique playstyle in battle[/b].

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/5e3ae9f7d9263f97dbea63f059eeb9375138fb4a.gif[/img]

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/dc3d364d796a68c515a3417de3418c415e4e0754.gif[/img]

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/26a06401d2a04ec8a59a71f465624ba663cdce0c.gif[/img]

In addition to all these set characteristics, some [b]dynamic[/b] aspects of the characters (e.g. stats) are affected by their state in the camp.
 
So, let’s dissect a battle skill.
Inside a row, a skill can be set to target 1 [b]CHARACTER, ALL CHARACTERS or 1 RANDOM CHARACTER[/b] & can be limited to target another character on a specific row (only front, or only back), or target [b]ANY row[/b].
Example: “Sniper Shot” can hit any enemy in any row…While “Hit n Run” can hit a RANDOM enemy in the Melee row.

Beside attacks, we also have buffs and debuffs which can change any parameter of the character with gain bonus ranks for [b]ACCURACY[/b] and [b]POWER[/b] rolls, but also for [b]CRITICAL[/b] chances, AP, Initiative, …etc.

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/465aa62773615363c66ea1dc971047b8fda94fd1.gif[/img]

We made the choice to exclude [b]HEALING[/b] skills from our game, for several reasons. It breaks immersion, we can’t imagine our characters taking time to magically heal themselves during an ambush in the woods… But more importantly, it would in the end artificially drag the length of the fights, and we most certainly don’t want that. As said our combats are designed to be [b]tactical[/b] but [b]quick[/b] and not the flow of our core management survival gameplay.
 
That’s it for now for our fighting system! See you next time for the following post on our [b]secondary characters[/b]!

·        [b]Mystic[/b]: Can buff and debuff
·        [b]Civilian[/b]: Disrupts the flow of the battle with their chaotic skills (row-changing, large damage range…)
 
The Battle Class determines the set of 5 activable skills the character has in battle.
They will also have a [b]Passive Ability[/b], which is independent from the Battle Class. It acts as a modifier to their behavior. Those different combinations mean [b]each character will have its unique playstyle in battle[/b].

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/5e3ae9f7d9263f97dbea63f059eeb9375138fb4a.gif[/img]

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/dc3d364d796a68c515a3417de3418c415e4e0754.gif[/img]

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/26a06401d2a04ec8a59a71f465624ba663cdce0c.gif[/img]

In addition to all these set characteristics, some [b]dynamic[/b] aspects of the characters (e.g. stats) are affected by their state in the camp.
 
So, let’s dissect a battle skill.
Inside a row, a skill can be set to target 1 [b]CHARACTER, ALL CHARACTERS or 1 RANDOM CHARACTER[/b] & can be limited to target another character on a specific row (only front, or only back), or target [b]ANY row[/b].
Example: “Sniper Shot” can hit any enemy in any row…While “Hit n Run” can hit a RANDOM enemy in the Melee row.

Beside attacks, we also have buffs and debuffs which can change any parameter of the character with gain bonus ranks for [b]ACCURACY[/b] and [b]POWER[/b] rolls, but also for [b]CRITICAL[/b] chances, AP, Initiative, …etc.

        [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/465aa62773615363c66ea1dc971047b8fda94fd1.gif[/img]

We made the choice to exclude [b]HEALING[/b] skills from our game, for several reasons. It breaks immersion, we can’t imagine our characters taking time to magically heal themselves during an ambush in the woods… But more importantly, it would in the end artificially drag the length of the fights, and we most certainly don’t want that. As said our combats are designed to be [b]tactical[/b] but [b]quick[/b] and not the flow of our core management survival gameplay.
 
That’s it for now for our fighting system! See you next time for the following post on our [b]secondary characters[/b]!

If you missed it, go take a look there: http://steamcommunity.com/games/573120/announcements/detail/3091029444970712518

As they discover the island they run aground on, they'll quickly understand that [b]they are not alone[/b]. They'll run into [b]various inhabitants[/b] that will be either [b]welcoming & warm[/b] or [b]aggressive & violent[/b]. Here we'll focus on some of the characters that might [b]join your camp[/b].

Those characters all ended up on this uncharted land for various reasons, some have fled like the family, others are here willingly. But [b]they all have something to offer[/b] if you understand their [b]strenghts & weaknesses[/b]!

                                                [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/eea42d42b72d2d770e95a60ba49ce3552b7ed0a7.png[/img]

We'll begin with Knut, who comes from a [b]danish tribe[/b] of fierce warriors. He is [b]married to Solveig[/b].
One cannot say that they were very lucky in life. Knut being forced out of the village warriors after he [b]lost his leg during a fight[/b], he became by necessity a bitter and below average [b]blacksmith[/b]. He also became very despotic with his family.
Then, their numerous children perished one after another to a typhus epidemic, none of them exceeding the age of twelve.
One day, the Jarl’s guards stormed into his house and bluntly took Knut and his wife to the Jarl, to endure his judgement. They were [b]expelled from the village[/b], condemned to run as exiles as far as possible to [b]avoid a certain death[/b].
Knut never accepted to explain to his wife the [b]true reasons behind their exile[/b].

                                                [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/d88629438e4f38920c4c22413892676dbd1636a5.png[/img]

Solveig comes from a [b]danish tribe[/b] of hardy people. She is [b]married to Knut[/b].
The youngest of a dozen brothers and sisters, the meals were scarce and the punishments were daily in her young days, but the [b]joy of growing up in a large family[/b] always warmed her big heart.
When she became of age, she married a strong and handsome warrior of the clan. Sadly, he wasn’t much home at first, leaving for months to rampage and pillage neighbouring rich shores, getting her pregnant each time he came back victorious.
This life was not perfect, but at least she was able to have this big family of her own that her heart desired.
That’s until most of their children died from a typhus epidemic and they got [b]expelled from the clan with no apparent reason[/b].
They sailed away with their [b]newborn child[/b] to a new, better life.

                                                [img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/d65ca25b83f9d789ec76f6684ad64d679cad1623.png[/img]

Gudrun is the Völva of the group. A Völva is a [b]female shaman[/b] who can [b]oversee the future[/b] and can [b]make dark magic[/b].
She’s the only member of the group who [b]arrived on the island[/b] who is here [b]willingly[/b]. She had seen what was happening to Eirik and his family, but she also [b]sensed some “defenses” coming from the island[/b]. She [b]KNEW[/b] she had to come to check out the place. However, she’s not sure how she ended up here, as she only remembers waking up on the beach after searching for the island for days.
Gudrun may seem old and useless, but she’s also a [b]quick-witted woman[/b], and a precious [b]mystic[/b] during [b]combat[/b]. What will her purpose be? Is she really seeing things related to the island, or is she just plain crazy?


Now that you've learnt a bit about them, you'll be more [b]prepared[/b] if you come across one of those survivors while exploring the island. See you next time for an [b]introduction to the battle system[/b] in Dead in Vinland!

notes.title: About the Characters: The Family
notes.notes:
Through your journey into Dead In Vinland, you will have [b]14 playable characters to choose from[/b]. They’re not just generic protagonists, each has his own backstory, some secrets to discover and special dialogs chain with other inhabitants of the camp.

[b]You start the game with only 4[/b] of them, a viking family exiled by force from their homeland. These are what you could call your [b]main characters[/b], on a system point of view.  These characters are super important. If you lose one of them, the other ones lose faith and the group is torn apart, [b]meaning instant game over[/b]. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/e533fda842bb882d7cc6f727a2c01eb9b4e00fbf.png[/img]

It will lead to many critical decisions, where the well-being of the family can lead to hard, “bad” decisions for the group, and vice-versa. Think of it like a cooperative board game, where some players have a special agenda of their own.

You’ll need to know all about those 4 characters because this is their story after all! So let’s introduce them:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/4d4d42969920b60e7909ba05d56d4d50cfe1a9f1.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/cc22441127d60c7176568ff139659c9c03da26ec.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/3901a142812ce6679ebee59c66f5838a9e453b70.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30295260/11a4f2b93330903da2716d11fd11b15dd8ea4b55.png[/img]

Now that you know them a little more, you’ll need to take into consideration their [b]personality, strengths / weaknesses[/b], & [b]their relationships to each other[/b] to try your best and survive on this uncharted island. notes.title: Dead in Vinland is a neat looking survive em up
notes.notes:
Dead in Vinland strikes me as The Banner Saga meets Darkest Dungeon. For a start, everyone looks utterly miserable. It’s a survival/management game with RPG elements where you play as a viking family, exiled and shipwrecked on an island. Is that island a peaceful place of bountiful splendour? Given the number of things you have to manage in order to keep your exiles from either dying or spiralling into a mental health crisis, I’d say not. There are people out to kill you, too.

It’ll be out in early 2018, and there’s a trailer below that shows off everything from camp management to RPG style choices to combat.

notes.title: Survive em up Dead in Vinland drops you on a desert island
notes.notes:
Dead in Vinland [official site] is a survival game about managing a band of exiles on a faraway island, and it looks pretty neat if you ask me. It’s the sequel (ish) to Dead in Bermuda, which put you in charge of eight plane crash survivors. You had to assign them tasks, research and craft new gear and explore the island. Dead in Vinland is not a direct follow up, but expect the same sort of thing in a fantasy settings: more cloth tunic than beach shorts.

Its hand-drawn art style looks great, like something straight out of a comic book. It’s out early next year.
